abstract: Just over five years ago, the SMPTE ST 2110 core standards were published. Building on the previously published work of the Video Services Forum (VSF TR-03:2015), the core ST 2110 specifications were the product of a drafting group with more than 200 participants, and typical meetings would garner a core of 60–70 attendees each week. The participants represented every major technology provider in the industry, and also many end-users, ensuring the standards covered the wide plethora of use-cases around the television production and distribution infrastructure universe.

authors.bio: John Mailhot is the chief technology officer of the Networking and Infrastructure Team with Imagine Communications. He has worked in the field of digital high-definition (HD) television systems since its North American inception in 1990. He began his career as part of the AT&T-Zenith Team, responsible for system architecture and integration of the digital spectrum-compatible high-definition television (DSC-HDTV) system prototype and then served as technical lead for the grand alliance encoder with Lucent Technologies. He has dual bachelor’s degrees in computer science and electrical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Cambridge, MA, and has been recognized as a SMPTE Fellow.

authors.bio: Bruce Devlinis the past standards vice president with SMPTE, the founder of Mr MXF, and has enjoyed C-level positions at media companies over the years. He is known for his work on MXF and is a recognized world expert in media files, formats, and IP transport systems.
